title: CHIP dataset
hook: The data this week comes from CHIP Dataset. Moore's law is the observation that the number of transistors in a dense integrated circuit (IC) doubles about every two years. Moore's law is an observation and projection of a historical trend. Rather than a law of physics, it is an empirical relationship linked to gains from experience in production. Paper for citation: Summarizing CPU and GPU Design Trends with Product Data Note that the authors prohibit resharing the dataset, so I've created a simple summary. You can easily download the full dataset at the bottom of: < Here are some interesting findings: - Moore's Law still holds, especially in GPUs. - Dannard Scaling is still valid in general. - CPUs have higher frequencies, but GPUs are catching up. - GPU performance doubles every 1.5 years.
